policies.quote: It is expressly forbidden to contribute to Gentoo any content that has been created with the assistance of Natural Language Processing artificial intelligence tools.
policies.scope_limits: Gentoo contributions and official Gentoo projects. Does not prohibit packaging AI-related software that is developed with such tools upstream.
policies.notes: Council motion of 2024-04-14. The motion can be revisited if a tool is shown not to pose copyright, ethical, and quality concerns.

policies.quote: The QEMU project thus requires that contributors refrain from using AI content generators on patches intended to be submitted to the project, and will decline any contribution if use of AI is either known or suspected.
policies.scope_limits: Does not apply to researching APIs or algorithms, static analysis, or debugging, when that output is not included in the contribution.
policies.notes: Pinned to docs/devel/code-provenance.rst at 2f127af408e1b4675662f9b8a0c3606f6565a1a7 (2026-05-22). Grounded in DCO copyright uncertainty.

policies.quote: Contributions must not include content generated by large language models or other probabilistic tools, including but not limited to Copilot or ChatGPT.
policies.scope_limits: Covers code, documentation, pull requests, issues, comments, and any other contribution to the Servo project.
policies.notes: Policy text lives in the Servo book, commit 36b3916fcee4ac10a0bd0b2c666fca19e388d1d6 (2026-04-04). The project says it may revise the policy later.

policies.quote: No LLM-generated content, whether it be code or prose.
policies.scope_limits: Also forbids paraphrasing LLM output, LLM editing or translation, sharing LLM brainstorming, using LLMs to find bugs, and discussing chatbot use.
policies.notes: Quoted from the rendered code of conduct. The page has no commit-pinned source link.

policies.quote: This project strictly forbids the usage of LLMs, agents, or any other AI tools for any kind of contribution.
policies.scope_limits: Issues, bug reports, patches, pull requests including descriptions, issue-tracker comments, code review, and translation.
policies.notes: CONTRIBUTING.md at 249aa5d6e667308fbf95ae5cfb40eba8177a802c (2026-07-01). Violators may be blocked without warning.

policies.quote: In the jsoup project, we do not accept code that has been generated in whole or part by AI/LLMs.
policies.scope_limits: Also rejects AI-written copy in issues, pull requests, and discussions. A machine translation to English is allowed only if the original text is included.

policies.quote: It is expressly forbidden to contribute to this project any content that has been created or derived with the assistance of AI tools.
policies.scope_limits: Includes AI linters, static analyzers, and summarizers used to derive a contribution. Accessibility tools such as a screen reader are allowed without disclosure when the contributor verifies the output.

policies.quote: Using AI tools to fix issues labelled as "good first issues" is forbidden.
policies.scope_limits: Other tool use is allowed with a human in the loop and a label on substantial tool-generated content. Unattended agents and automated review comments without human review are not allowed.
policies.notes: llvm/docs/AIToolPolicy.md at 28d90b4824d5b485c891b1fcfc5b79add6052916 (2026-09-23). The quoted sentence is bold in the Markdown source.

policies.quote: Code generated by a large language model or similar technology, such as GitHub/Microsoft's Copilot, OpenAI's ChatGPT, or Facebook/Meta's Code Llama, is presumed to be tainted code, and must not be committed without prior written approval by core.
policies.scope_limits: LLM-generated code may be committed only with prior written approval by core. The guidelines do not describe a general disclosure trailer.
policies.notes: Quoted from the public commit guidelines. Disclosure here means the approval request to core, not a standing public trailer.

policies.quote: Unless you are a maintainer, you may only have one AI-assisted/generated pull request open at a time.
policies.scope_limits: Disclosure of the tool or model is required. AI must not be an author, co-author, committer, signatory, or Assisted-by/Co-developed-by trailer. Review replies must be written by the human.

policies.quote: Disclose which AI tools were used and what they were used for (e.g., generating code, drafting commit messages, writing documentation).
policies.scope_limits: Automated AI reviews must not be requested on pull requests to the Django repository. Using those tools in a private fork before submission is allowed.
policies.notes: docs/internals/contributing/writing-code/submitting-patches.txt at 862ade3409ceaa8ec5305e6f5aa26ee0e553cf02. The word Disclose is bold in the source.

policies.quote: If you used AI tools in preparing your PR, you must disclose this in the description of your PR.
policies.scope_limits: Large AI-generated pull requests and AI-generated commit messages are not allowed. assisted-by and co-developed trailers are not allowed. Review replies must not rely on AI tools.
policies.notes: Policy is in kubernetes/community, not the main code repository. pull-requests.md at 4ca30c408449b4589332a8af9e59a3170db5eb49 (2026-04-15).

policies.quote: Contributions should include an Assisted-by tag in the following format: Assisted-by: LLM [TOOL1] [TOOL2]
policies.scope_limits: Only a human may add Signed-off-by. Trivial typing aids, spelling fixes, and mechanical reformatting are outside the separate tool-generated-content guidelines.
policies.notes: Documentation/process/coding-assistants.rst at 72fdff1416e280e2baaa3cca69574defb998437e (merged 2026-08-20). The source uses an RST literal block after format.

policies.quote: Contributions made with the assistance of AI tools are welcome, but contributors must use them responsibly and disclose that use clearly.
policies.scope_limits: AI must not be used to reply to review questions. Contributors must be able to explain, defend, and revise the change themselves.
policies.notes: CONTRIBUTING.md at b3b9c4903e0e053941c0f3a0766a4016b9a0dac6 (2026-07-20). Welcome is conditional on disclosure, so this is not an undisclosed-use policy.

policies.quote: Disclosure of the use of AI tools in the PR description is appreciated, while not required.
policies.scope_limits: Acceptable uses named in the guide include comments (especially in a non-native language), understanding existing code, and supplementing contributor knowledge. The author must still explain the change in their own words.
policies.notes: Policy is in the Python Developer's Guide, commit 0d87d7ede987867f64a64053fdf41fd45b7a918d (2026-07-21), not in the CPython tree itself. Disclosure is optional, which is why the stance is welcomes rather than allows_with_disclosure.

takeaways: Seven of these fifteen policies forbid AI-assisted contributions, and the ban usually covers more than code: issues, reviews, comments, and sometimes translation (yt-dlp, Zig, Servo, jsoup).
Where AI help is allowed, a human who understands the change is required. Disclosure is the usual extra gate, as in Django, Kubernetes, Gitea, and the kernel Assisted-by trailer.

Allowed does not mean unlimited. LLVM forbids AI fixes on good-first-issue, NetBSD treats model output as tainted unless core approves it in writing, and Homebrew caps non-maintainers at one open AI-assisted pull request.
CPython is the permissive case in this set: disclosure is appreciated and not required, while the author must still review the work and explain it.
The written reasons repeat. License provenance drives the bans at QEMU, Gentoo, and man-pages, and maintainer review time drives the limits at Servo, Django, and Homebrew.
